results.content: Unser Artikel zum Selbstverständnis von Gründerinnen ist Open Access bei Springer veröffentlicht und damit nun für alle einlesbar! 📄 How women tech founders navigate visibility in the startup ecosystem 2026 has started on a high note: our article “Doing, redoing, or undoing gender of women tech founders in Germany” has just been published in the International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal by Springer Nature 🎉 Together with Melanie Slavici, I examined how women tech founders in Germany navigate gender and visibility. This research emerged from our project on the visibility of female founders, funded by the German Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt and embedded in the Metavorhaben „Innovative Frauen im Fokus“ (meta-IFiF). When I started the Gates Foundation, I saw an opportunity to save and improve millions of lives because critical areas like children’s health were getting so little money. A new report and two recent announcements are reminders of the important role of the pharmaceutical industry, especially in helping save the lives of people in poor countries. The index ranks 20 of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies on their efforts to make sure that medicines are made for and reach people in developing countries. One example of progress on access is the announcement by GlaxoSmithKline and Pfizer Inc. that they will accelerate production and distribution of new vaccines against pneumococcal disease, which kills 1.6 million people a year—mostly in developing countries, and half of them children under the age of five.
